issues.description: The UML/problem statement specifies the attribute numberOfInscribedStudents as type int, but the provided solution declares it as long. This also forces the constructor and getter/setter to use long, contradicting the specified API contract and likely breaking student submissions that follow the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the artifacts: preferably change the solution (field declaration and all related signatures) to use int for numberOfInscribedStudents. If long is intended, update the UML/problem statement (and any tests) to specify long consistently.

issues.description: In the solution, getTotalNumberOfStudents() is declared to return int but computes numberOfGuestStudents (int) + numberOfInscribedStudents (long). In Java this expression is long, so returning it as int causes a compilation error without an explicit cast. This indicates the solution is inconsistent with the intended types in the specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the type inconsistency so the method compiles and matches the spec: change numberOfInscribedStudents to int (preferred, matching UML) so the sum is int, or alternatively change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long and update the UML/problem statement accordingly.
